agent.description: The id the agent goes by: the id of its `acp_harness` provider when it has one (`claude`), else the lower-case name of its source. Every other provider and source of the agent names it this way.

title.description: Its name for people, such as `Claude`.

program.description: The program's name for people, such as `Claude Code`; absent when it is the title.

vendor.description: The vendor a session on it is stamped with (`AGENTS_VENDOR`), such as `anthropic`; absent for an agent with none.

aos.description: The agent's id in the standard registry of harnesses (`claude-code`); absent when the registry has none.

model_variable.description: The variable the running model is read from in the agent's environment (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`).

tool_name.description: Where the agent puts a tool's own name in a tool call's `_meta`, as a JSON pointer below `_meta` (`/claudeCode/toolName`); absent for an agent whose tool call title is the name.

skills_folder.description: The folder below a project where the agent reads skills from (`.claude/skills`), for a source of skills to be searched there.

context_files.description: The files of a project's context the agent loads for itself, as paths below a directory written with `/` (`AGENTS.md`), so the host does not give it the same text a second time. Empty for an agent that loads none of the standard names.

home_variable.description: The variable that names the folder the agent keeps its own files in (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), which a person may point elsewhere.

home_folder.description: That folder when the variable is not set, below the person's home (`.claude`).

home_context_files.description: The files in that folder the agent loads as the person's own instructions, as paths below it written with `/` (`CLAUDE.md`).

login_files.description: The files in that folder the agent keeps its own sign-in in (`.credentials.json`), as paths below it written with `/`. The host lists the agent's own login as the account `local` only when one of them is there and not empty; an agent that lists none keeps it somewhere a file does not say (a keyring), so its `local` account is always listed.

login_env.description: The variables of the host's environment that sign the agent in by themselves (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), which the program takes in place of its stored login. A session started where one is set and not empty is signed in, so the account `local` is listed for it and says which variable it is; the value is never read beyond that.

title.description: What a person reads for it, such as `Anthropic API`.

standards.description: The credential standards that are the vendor's own, with their names for people.

names.description: The names the agent reports for itself in ACP's `initialize` (`agentInfo.name`), which tell its sessions apart.

markers.description: The keys of `initialize`'s `_meta` that are `true` for this agent and no other, for one that reports no `agentInfo` name.

id.description: The mode's id, as the agent names it.

title.description: What a person reads for it.

modes.description: The modes the agent is known to offer before it has run.

endpoints.description: The `https` addresses the agent's program reaches while it runs (`https://api.anthropic.com/`): its model API and login hosts. The host asks the system's proxy about each, to choose the proxy the program is started with.

mark.description: Its mark as SVG text: `path` elements with a `d` and an optional `fill`, in the `viewBox`'s square. A path with no `fill`, or `currentColor`, is drawn in the text's colour. At most [`MAX_DOCUMENT_TEXT`] characters.

look.description: Its look as a JSON document with an `id`, a `label`, the agent's `vendor` and, for `light` and `dark`, colour tokens.

title.description: What a person reads for it, such as `Anthropic API`.

id.description: The mode's id, as the agent names it.

title.description: What a person reads for it.

key.description: The credential that holds the file's text.

file.description: The file's name in the account's directory.

name.description: The program's file name without its extension, in lower case (`bash`, `pwsh`).

wsl.description: Whether it is the one the Windows Subsystem for Linux starts.

windows.description: Whether the host runs on Windows.

env.description: The variables that make the agent use the shell.

notice.description: Why the agent does not use it, in words, when it cannot be told.

home.description: The folder the program keeps them in, or none for where the program itself looks.

limit.description: The most files to look at.

peek.description: How many of the newest files are read for their title and folder.

id.description: The session's id as the program names it.

updated_ms.description: When it last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

title.description: The first thing the person said in it, tidy and short.

cwd.description: The folder the session worked in.

home.description: The folder they were read from, when there is one.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of a session file [`AgentVendor::session_history`] takes.

id.description: The session's id as the program names it.

updated_ms.description: When it last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

title.description: The first thing the person said in it, tidy and short.

cwd.description: The folder the session worked in.

files.description: The session files found, the newest first.

session.description: The id the history's session is given (a UUID).

history.description: The history in the standard session-history format: its JSON lines.

title.description: The first thing the person said in the session, tidy and short.

path.description: The file's path below the folder.

folder.description: The plugin's folder below the folder the host wrote, `/`-separated; empty for that folder itself.

meta.description: What the session request's `_meta` gains, as an object: it is merged into the request's, objects key by key and lists by appending. A string that is exactly [`PLUGIN_PATH`] becomes the folder's absolute path.

additional_directories.description: Whether the agent's `initialize` says it takes ACP's `additionalDirectories`.

folder.description: The folder, below the one the host writes, that holds a skill's own folder: a skill `name` is written at `<folder>/<name>/...`.

path.description: The file's path below the folder.

files.description: The files written beside the skills, such as a plugin's manifest.

folder.description: The plugin's folder below the folder the host wrote, `/`-separated; empty for that folder itself.

meta.description: What the session request's `_meta` gains, as an object: it is merged into the request's, objects key by key and lists by appending. A string that is exactly [`PLUGIN_PATH`] becomes the folder's absolute path.

plugin.description: The folder the agent loads as a plugin, when it takes skills in one.

directory.description: Whether the folder the host wrote is given to the session as an additional directory.

how.description: What the report says of each skill, in words; `{name}` is the skill's name.

x-enum-labels.start: A session started again or was compacted into or cleared.
x-enum-labels.pre-compact: A compaction is about to run, which the command's failure stops.
x-enum-labels.batch: A batch of tool calls ended.
x-enum-labels.pre-tool: One of the agent's own tools is about to run (a tool [`ToolHook::tools`] names): the command reads the agent's payload on standard input and prints the answer the agent reads on standard output. A command that fails, or exits with any status but 0, refuses the call.

kind.description: What it reports: `start` (a session started again or was compacted into or cleared), `pre-compact` (a compaction is about to run, which the command's failure stops), or `batch` (a batch of tool calls ended).

command.description: The command line, quoted for a POSIX shell, that reports it to the host.

kind.description: What it reports: `start` (a session started again or was compacted into or cleared), `pre-compact` (a compaction is about to run, which the command's failure stops), or `batch` (a batch of tool calls ended).

command.description: The command line, quoted for a POSIX shell, that reports it to the host.

commands.description: One command for each moment to be reported.

timeout_seconds.description: The longest, in seconds, the host may take to answer one.

path.description: The file's path below the folder.

files.description: The files written, below the folder the host made for the session.

folder.description: The plugin's folder below the folder the host wrote, `/`-separated; empty for that folder itself.

meta.description: What the session request's `_meta` gains, as an object: it is merged into the request's, objects key by key and lists by appending. A string that is exactly [`PLUGIN_PATH`] becomes the folder's absolute path.

plugin.description: How the session request loads them.

event.description: The event: `cd` (the working directory changed), `pre-compact` or `session-start`.

reason.description: For `session-start`, why a session starts that ACP does not show: `compact` or `clear`.

text.description: How it fires, or why it cannot, in words.

name.description: Its name, as the agent's payload gives it.

x-enum-labels.shell: Runs a shell command, which [`HookTool::command`] names in its input.
x-enum-labels.files: Reads, writes, edits, searches or lists files.
x-enum-labels.pass: Acts on nothing of the computer it runs on (a list of tasks, a question to the person, a search of the web): it runs as it is, wherever the session's tools are served from.

command.description: For a shell: the key of its input that holds the command.

shell.description: For a shell: the shell the command is written for.

word.description: The word the agent's payload carries (`dontAsk`).

mode.description: The mode: `manual` (asks), `accept_edits`, `auto`, `plan`, `bypass`, or `dont_ask` (refuses what no rule allows).

name.description: Its name, as the agent's payload gives it.

x-enum-labels.shell: Runs a shell command, which [`HookTool::command`] names in its input.
x-enum-labels.files: Reads, writes, edits, searches or lists files.
x-enum-labels.pass: Acts on nothing of the computer it runs on (a list of tasks, a question to the person, a search of the web): it runs as it is, wherever the session's tools are served from.

command.description: For a shell: the key of its input that holds the command.

shell.description: For a shell: the shell the command is written for.

tools.description: The agent's tools by what they do. The hook runs before every tool: one listed here as a shell is taken over, one that passes runs as it is, and every other (a file tool, a tool not listed, one the agent adds later) is refused.

pass_prefixes.description: The beginnings of tool names that pass as [`ToolRole::Pass`] tools do (the tools of the MCP servers a session is given).

name_at.description: Where the payload names the tool.

input_at.description: Where the payload holds the tool's input, an object.

mode_at.description: Where the payload says the agent's permission mode, when it does.

word.description: The word the agent's payload carries (`dontAsk`).

mode.description: The mode: `manual` (asks), `accept_edits`, `auto`, `plan`, `bypass`, or `dont_ask` (refuses what no rule allows).

modes.description: The agent's words for its modes.

deny.description: The answer that refuses the call, as JSON text.

rewrite.description: The answer that changes the call's input and decides nothing, so the agent's own rules and mode still decide whether it runs, as JSON text.

rewrite_input_at.description: Where the new input goes in [`Self::rewrite`].

harness.description: The agent's id in the standard registry of harnesses, which names its table of words.

at_launch.description: Whether a program the host starts itself is given the access in its arguments, variables and session `_meta`; false when the agent takes it in each session's request.

kind.description: The agent's own account kind that takes an address and a secret.

credential.description: The key of that kind's credentials that holds the bearer.

address.description: The key of its settings that holds the address; absent when the agent reads it from a file in its folder ([`AgentVendor::gateway_files`]).

suffix.description: What follows the gateway's address in the address the agent is given (`/v1`).

fixed.description: Settings of that kind the account fixes, each a key and its value.

managed.description: The launch settings of the copy of the agent the Store installed, each a name and its text; empty when there is none. A setting that is an absolute path names a file inside that copy.

protected.description: The places the person's configuration says a session may not read or change, when it says any; absent when it says nothing.
